stem:
Dinitrogen pentoxide, $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$, is dissolved in an inert solvent (solv) and the rate of decomposition of $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ is investigated. This reaction produces nitrogen dioxide, which remains in solution, and oxygen gas.

$$\text{N}_2\text{O}_5(\text{solv}) \rightarrow 2\text{NO}_2(\text{solv}) + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2(\text{g})$$

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest a method by which the rate of this reaction could be followed.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
In a separate experiment, the rate of the decomposition of $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5(\text{g})$ is investigated.

$$\text{N}_2\text{O}_5(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{NO}_2(\text{g}) + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2(\text{g})$$

The graph shows the results obtained.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

The reaction is first order with respect to $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$. This can be confirmed from the graph using half-lives.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Explain the term *half-life of a reaction*.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the half-life of this reaction. Show your working on the graph.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Suggest the effect on the half-life of this reaction if the initial concentration of $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ is halved.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Use the graph in 5(b) to determine the rate of reaction at 200 s. Show your working.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The rate equation for this reaction is shown.

$\text{rate} = k[\text{N}_2\text{O}_5]$

Use your answer to (c)(i) to calculate the value of the rate constant, $k$, for this reaction and state its units.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Nitrogen dioxide reacts with ozone, $\text{O}_3$, as shown.

$$2\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_3 \rightarrow \text{N}_2\text{O}_5 + \text{O}_2$$

The rate equation for this reaction is $\text{rate} = k[\text{NO}_2][\text{O}_3]$.

Suggest a possible two-step mechanism for this reaction.
